title: Walsh character on an extended coordinate set
statement:
Let $S \subseteq [n]$, let $x \in \{0,1\}^n$, and let $b$ be a bit. Write $(x,b) \in \{0,1\}^{n+1}$ for the point obtained by appending $b$ as the final coordinate, and let $S' \subseteq [n+1]$ be the image of $S$ under the inclusion $[n] \hookrightarrow [n+1]$ of the first $n$ coordinates, together with the new last coordinate $n+1$. Then
\[
  \chi_{S'}(x,b) \;=\; \sigma(b)\,\chi_S(x),
\]
where $\sigma$ is the sign encoding; that is, adjoining the last coordinate to the lifted index set multiplies the Walsh character by the sign of $b$.
hypotheses_covered: S is a subset of the first n coordinates
x is a point of the n-dimensional cube
index set is the lift of S together with the last coordinate
evaluation point extends x by appending b
replaced:
For $S \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,n$, a point $x$, and a bit $b$, adjoining the last
coordinate to the lifted set multiplies the character by the sign of $b$:
\[
  \chi_{\,\mathrm{castSucc}(S)\cup\{\mathrm{last}\,n\}}(\mathrm{snoc}\,x\,b)
  = (-1)^{b}\,\chi_S(x),
\]
where $(-1)^b$ denotes \texttt{boolToSign}\,$b$.
